title: Sea View, Sea Road, Blackrock, Co. Louth, A91CD34
seoTitle: Sea View, Sea Road, Blackrock, Co. Louth, A91CD34
description:
A charming period home enjoying sea views

Sea View occupies an enviable position at the end of a terrace on Sea Road, directly facing The Priests Beach and open to an outlook that few homes along this coastline can rival. Across the road lies a well-regarded sea swimming location, and the Cooley Mountains form a compelling backdrop to the north-east. The home extends to 124.9 sq m, is available immediately, and carries the kind of unhurried character that comes with a well-kept, established property — with some original period features lending warmth and texture throughout.

At ground level, the accommodation flows from a generous kitchen and breakfast room through to a formal dining room that readily adapts to a home office or reading room, a comfortable sitting room, a utility room, and a guest WC. The layout is practical and well-proportioned, with each room serving a clear purpose without feeling contrived. A large landing or office area at upper level adds valuable flexible space, particularly suited to those working from home or in need of a quiet study. 

All four bedrooms are positioned to benefit from sea views, a distinction that sets the property apart from comparable properties in the area. Waking to open water each morning is not a secondary benefit here — it is the defining quality of the home. A family bathroom serves the upper floor, and the overall condition of the accommodation means a new owner can settle in without delay, while still having scope to add their own mark over time.

Outside, a private rear garden offers a sunny and sheltered seating area, well away from passing traffic and not overlooked. Parking to the side of the house is a practical asset in a coastal village setting. The combination of outlook, orientation, village position, and ready availability makes Sea View a genuinely compelling prospect for those seeking a lifestyle change, a considered downsizer move, or a coastal base within realistic reach of Dublin and Belfast.

Sea Road is widely regarded as one of Blackrock's most sought-after residential addresses, occupying a spectacular seafront setting overlooking Dundalk Bay with uninterrupted views across the water towards the Cooley and Mourne Mountains. The location perfectly balances the tranquillity of coastal living with the convenience of an excellent range of amenities within easy reach.

Blackrock is a thriving and welcoming seaside village renowned for its attractive promenade, strong community spirit and exceptional lifestyle offering. A superb selection of boutique shops, independent cafés, artisan bakeries and well-regarded restaurants make the village a vibrant destination for both residents and visitors alike. The village also boasts a sandy beach, playgrounds, sports facilities and a year-round programme of community events, creating an enviably family-friendly environment.

Dundalk, just 4 km away, provides a comprehensive range of retail, commercial and cultural amenities, while Drogheda (34 km), Ireland's largest town, offers an extensive array of shopping, dining and leisure facilities.

The area is particularly well served by recreational amenities. Dundalk Stadium (7.5 km), Ireland's only all-weather horse and greyhound racing venue, is close by, while golf enthusiasts are spoilt for choice with Dundalk Golf Club, Greenore Golf Club, Ardee Golf Club and the renowned County Louth Golf Club in Baltray (33 km), one of Ireland's most celebrated championship links courses. The surrounding coastline also offers excellent opportunities for sailing, water sports, sea swimming and scenic coastal walks.

Families are well catered for with a wide choice of excellent educational facilities. Blackrock is served by several highly regarded primary schools, while secondary education options in Dundalk include Dundalk Grammar School and a number of established public and private schools. Dundalk Institute of Technology provides a respected third-level education offering for the wider region.

Transport connections are excellent. The M1 motorway (Junction 16) is approximately 4 km away, providing direct access to Dublin (77 km) and Belfast (84 km). Dublin Airport is approximately 72 km south of the property, while Dundalk Railway Station (4 km) offers regular intercity services to both Dublin and Belfast, making the area particularly attractive for commuters.
